bull.b: The latest annual balance sheet indicates materially lower leverage, with positive equity and no reported debt. This gives Merlin more financial flexibility than in 2024 and reduces current interest and repayment pressure, although the sharp change still requires careful assessment of its durability.

Appointing an executive with public sector, defense technology, aerospace, and industry-body experience could strengthen operational leadership in Merlin’s target markets. His background may support customer engagement and execution over the next several quarters, though benefits depend on business recovery.

Separating the President and CEO roles can create clearer accountability between day-to-day execution and board-level leadership. The disclosure of no special arrangements or related-party transactions also supports a more conventional governance process around this leadership transition.

bear.b: Revenue reaching zero represents a severe operational disruption and leaves no demonstrated recurring sales base from which to support future growth. Until revenue is re-established and sustained, Merlin’s market position, business model viability, and ability to generate durable margins remain highly uncertain.

Negative operating and free cash flow across multiple annual periods shows that the business has not consistently funded itself through operations. Continued cash burn can require external funding and restrict investment capacity, making recovery more dependent on restoring operating receipts.

Positive net income alongside negative operating profit suggests that reported earnings were not driven by a stable improvement in core operations. Combined with prior deep losses, this volatility weakens confidence in sustainable profitability and makes future earnings power difficult to assess.
